newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony president expects record 96/97 sales, profits.
newsitem.headline: Sony president expects record 96/97 sales, profits.

text.p: Sony Corp president Nobuyuki Idei said he expects group sales and operating profits to reach record highs in the current business year to the end of March.

"We will definitely see record high group sales and operating profits in the current business year," Idei said in an interview. "Many digital products, such as minidiscs and camcorders, are selling very fast.
Sony said last November that it expected group sales to rise 16 percent to 5.35 trillion yen and group operating profit to soar 30 percent to 305 billion yen in 1996/97, both record highs.
Asked about the prospects for the year starting April 1, Idei said there are some uncertainties, but Sony is now gaining momentum and that could help its business.
"It is difficult for a giant company like Sony to continue growth (in profits) of more than 10 percent," Idei said.

"But Sony is gathering momentum and that might help." Analysts expect the yen's weakening, which boosted Sony's profits this year, to come to a halt in the next business year and for price declines of audio-visual products to continue on the global market.
Idei said Sony's task in the next fiscal year is to launch a new generation of minidiscs, camcorders and other digital audio-visual products in overseas markets.
